I think it's a fallacy to assume a cryptocurrency must always have active devs for it to not 'be in a bubble'.

Demand for non-fiat is the application for $DOGE & friends.
The biggest use case for Dogecoin is that a random small business owner can accept it as payment and make it to the top of Reddit for a day.

It's funny how the same tech can fail once, but work years later.

Anyone remember tipping using Dogecoin on Reddit? That dust probably turned into like $40k during the bull peak.
